summary: A compact, free public square in Chiang Mai’s Old City, centered on the bronze Three Kings Monument in front of the former provincial hall, now the Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre. Best treated as a short heritage stop and meeting point, paired with the nearby municipal museums rather than a standalone half-day attraction.
whyGo: See the monument honoring Mangrai, Ngam Mueang and Ram Khamhaeng, with the old civic building as a backdrop.
Use the central location to connect a museum visit with nearby Old City temples and streets.
bestFor: A brief, low-cost Old City orientation stop
Travelers interested in Lanna history or local civic life
Pairing with the Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre
skipIf: You need a full indoor attraction or extensive interpretation at the monument itself.
You are visiting only to see the adjacent museum on Monday or Tuesday, when the municipal heritage centre network lists itself as closed.
duration: Allow 15–30 minutes for the square and photos; add 1–2 hours if visiting the adjacent museum (planning estimate).
cost: The monument precinct is free according to Thailand’s tourism directory. The adjacent City Heritage Centre network lists adult admission at ฿20 and child admission at ฿10; confirm the specific museum and current price before setting out.
hours: The monument is an open civic square, but a dependable official public-hours listing was not found. The adjacent City Heritage Centre network lists Wed–Sun, 08:30–16:30, closed Mon–Tue; museum hours do not necessarily apply to the square.
bestTime: Visit in the morning or late afternoon for a comfortable outdoor stop and softer light. December is in Chiang Mai’s cooler season, but afternoons can still feel warm; use the square as a flexible walk break.
gettingThere: At the Old City’s central Phra Pok Klao Road, in front of the former city hall. It is walkable from several central Old City sights; use a tuk-tuk or app taxi for a direct drop-off if needed. Confirm the exact pin with your map app.
booking: No booking or ticket is indicated for the public monument square. Bookings are not mentioned on the municipal heritage centre contact page; check directly with the specific museum if combining visits.
accessibility: Thailand’s tourism directory lists disability facilities, but the precise provision at the monument is unclear. The outdoor square is a short, central stop; confirm curb-free access and surface conditions locally. Museum access may differ.
practicalTips: Treat the monument respectfully; visitors commonly pay homage here, and offerings may be present.
Combine with the adjacent museum while it is open Wed–Sun, then continue to nearby temples on foot.
The square is exposed to sun and rain; carry water and have a light rain layer in December.
decemberNotes: No confirmed December 2026 event or special closure notice was found. This remains a short outdoor stop that fits easily around museum hours and other Old City visits; check municipal notices shortly before travel for ceremonies or temporary access changes.
uncertainties: No reliable official opening-hours schedule for the outdoor precinct was located; a tourism directory displays hours in an ambiguous format, so they are not repeated here.
The municipal centre page gives network hours and prices but does not clearly specify which individual museum these apply to.
December 2026 events, temporary closures and detailed step-free access are unconfirmed.
